story.title: OpenAI Delays Release of New AI Model Due to Safety Concerns
story.summary: OpenAI has decided not to release its new GPT-6.1 Astra model, citing safety concerns. This decision aligns with a growing industry trend to pause the development of advanced AI systems until adequate safety measures are established. Industry leaders have raised alarms about the risks associated with increasingly powerful AI technologies.

timeline_highlights.title: Anthropic Researcher Warns of AI Threat to Humanity
timeline_highlights.summary: A researcher from Anthropic has stated there is more than a 10% chance that artificial intelligence could lead to human extinction within the next decade. This warning follows the resignation of a colleague who expressed similar concerns about the rapid development of superintelligent AI that may surpass human control. Experts emphasize the seriousness of these risks, given their access to unreleased AI systems.
key_facts: Anthropic researcher estimates over 10% chance AI could kill all humans.
Concerns arise from the rapid advancement of AI technology.
A colleague resigned over fears of out-of-control AI.

event_overview.title: About AI Safety
event_overview.subject: AI Safety
event_overview.summary: AI safety is a broad research, engineering, and governance field concerned with reducing the risk that artificial-intelligence systems cause harm, whether through failures, misuse, or unintended behavior. It is not a single institution or legally uniform regime: governments, international organizations, standards bodies, companies, and researchers use different voluntary frameworks, declarations, and laws to address risks across an AI system’s lifecycle.

facts.label: Nature and purpose
facts.value: AI safety encompasses technical evaluation and risk management as well as governance efforts intended to make AI systems trustworthy, secure, resilient, and less likely to cause unreasonable harm.

facts.label: U.S. risk-management framework
facts.value: The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology released AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 on January 26, 2023. It is intended for voluntary use in managing risks to individuals, organizations, and society and in incorporating trustworthiness into AI design, development, use, and evaluation.

facts.label: Core risk-management format
facts.value: NIST’s AI RMF organizes risk-management activity around four functions—govern, map, measure, and manage—and describes risk management as continuous across the AI lifecycle rather than a one-time compliance exercise.

facts.label: International coordination
facts.value: At the UK-hosted AI Safety Summit at Bletchley Park, Buckinghamshire, on November 1–2, 2023, participating countries agreed the Bletchley Declaration, which called for international cooperation on the opportunities and risks of frontier AI, including risks from misuse and loss of control.

facts.label: Global governance context
facts.value: The UN Secretary-General’s High-level Advisory Body on AI operated from October 26, 2023 for 12 months and issued its 2024 final report proposing internationally inclusive arrangements to address AI-related risks and share AI’s benefits; the report underscored that no single global AI-governance framework existed.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a limited set of prominent September 2026 corporate, political, and alleged legal developments related to AI-safety debate; it does not aim to catalog the full technical research field, all AI incidents, or every national and international policy initiative.

related_stories.title: Tragic Incident in Calais: Child and Two Women Die During Channel Crossing
related_stories.summary: A 10-year-old boy and two women in their thirties died while attempting to cross the English Channel from France. The incident occurred on an overcrowded boat carrying more than 100 people, which faced difficulties off the northern French coast. Authorities reported that the victims were likely trampled during the chaos as passengers sought help.

related_stories.title: Congolese Politician Beaten After Promoting Ebola Awareness
related_stories.summary: Marie-Celestin Karondwa, a politician from the ruling UDPS party in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, was beaten on Sunday after advocating for Ebola awareness during a radio interview. The incident occurred in Butembo, a region experiencing an Ebola outbreak, as residents reacted violently to his message promoting disease prevention measures.

related_stories.title: Cornell University Rape Case Reopened Following Lawsuit
related_stories.summary: Prosecutors have reopened the investigation into a woman's allegations of sexual assault at Cornell University, which she claims occurred in 2024. This decision follows her filing of a civil lawsuit, in which she alleges she was drugged and raped at a fraternity house.
